newsitem.title: USA: Bon-Ton Stores losses shrink, to close 5 stores.
newsitem.headline: Bon-Ton Stores losses shrink, to close 5 stores.

text.p: The Bon-Ton Stores Inc., a struggling department store chain, said Thursday its losses shrank in the quarter, and it will close five stores as of Jan. 11.

The York, Pa.-based retailer said its net losses declined to $242,000, or 2 cents a share, in the quarter ended Nov. 2, from $3.3 million, or 30 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Sales grew to $148.4 million from $138.9 million.
The company said the closures are part of its effort to eliminate underperforming assets, leaving it with 64 stores.
The stores affected are in Johnstown, Frackville and Washington, Penn.; Cortland, N.Y.; and Fairmont, West Va.
As previously announced, the Pennsylvania and West Virginia stores, acquired from Hess Department Stores Inc. in September 1994, had been targeted for short-term operations only.
"Our store closure review is now complete and there are no plans to close additional stores in fiscal 1996," the company said.
Bon-Ton's department stores carry brand-name fashions and accessories for women, men and children, as well as home furnishings.
Its stock closed Wednesday at $5.25 on Nasdaq.
